titulo: Quiz — The compliment that reaches the kitchen
subtitulo: Both sentences need a noun in them
introPt: A traveller sends praise through to the kitchen, then gets a cold plate sorted in one sentence.
cenario: Mid-meal in a small dining room, one good plate and one cold one.

dialogo.es: 焼き魚がとても美味しかったです。ごちそうさまでした。
dialogo.pt: The grilled fish was really delicious. Thank you for the meal.
dialogo.tts: 焼き魚がとても美味しかったです。ごちそうさまでした。

dialogo.es: ありがとうございます。板前に伝えます。喜びます。
dialogo.pt: Thank you. I'll tell the cook, he'll be pleased.
dialogo.tts: ありがとうございます。板前に伝えます。喜びます。

dialogo.es: すみません、これ、冷たいです。
dialogo.tts: すみません、これ、冷たいです。

dialogo.es: あ、失礼しました。すぐ温め直します。
dialogo.pt: Oh sorry, I'll heat it again right away.
dialogo.tts: あ、失礼しました。すぐ温め直します。

perguntas.pergunta: What makes praise travel to the kitchen?
perguntas.explica: Nobody can carry oishii into a kitchen. They can carry yaki-zakana — the grilled fish.

perguntas.pergunta: How is the sentence about the cold plate built?
opcoes: Sumimasen, then the fact, then stop
Apology, the fact, then another apology
A full account of the evening so far
Say nothing and write it up later
perguntas.explica: Sumimasen, kore, tsumetai desu — six words is a complete request. The shorter it is, the faster the plate moves.

perguntas.pergunta: Why does stacking apologies on top backfire?
opcoes: It is too formal for a dining room
It buries the fact and signals you expect an argument
perguntas.explica: A flat, warm, factual sentence is heard as information instead.

perguntas.pergunta: The reply to your compliment is short — tsutaemasu — and then he walks off. That means:
opcoes: The reply is brief by convention; the message still goes through
You should ask for the chef
perguntas.explica: The part that matters happens out of your sight, in the kitchen. Length of reply measures nothing.

perguntas.pergunta: The strongest compliment available to you is:
perguntas.explica: A room that feeds the same neighbourhood every week measures its work in the people who come back.
